findings.evidence: `ExponentialShift.lean:126-127` proves `(S.expShift lambda).HasGrowthBound (ω - lambda) M`, and `GrowthBound.lean:80-83` already has `HasGrowthBound.mono_omega`, so the exact `omega = lambda` assumption at `ExponentialShift.lean:148-149` is stronger than the natural contraction criterion.
findings.fix: Generalize the constructor to take `{ω lambda : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω 1) (hω : ω ≤ lambda)` and prove contractivity from `hb.expShift` plus `ω - lambda ≤ 0`; keep the exact `(lambda,1)` case as a derived convenience if desired.
findings.issue: `expShiftContraction` only accepts `hb : S.HasGrowthBound lambda 1`, but shifting by any `lambda` at least a known unit growth exponent is already contractive; the same over-specialized hypothesis is repeated in the helper lemmas at lines 161 and 169.

summary: The exponential shift itself is at the right level, but the contraction packaging is unnecessarily exact in the growth exponent.
